# pragma-docs

A React application with server-side rendering and routing, generated by
`@canonical/summon`. It is built on Canonical's shared design system, router, and
SSR packages, and ships SSR on two runtimes (Bun and Node), file-based routing, a
component library wired to design tokens, and Storybook.

## Quick start

```bash
bun install
bun run dev:bun      # SSR dev server with HMR, on http://localhost:5174
```

Edit anything under `src/` and the page hot-reloads. To check the production
build before shipping, run `bun run preview:bun` instead.

## Running the app

The server scripts form a **2×3 matrix** — two modes (development and preview)
across three targets (a client-only SPA, SSR on Bun, SSR on Node/Express):

|                  | `dev` — transform, HMR | `preview` — compiled, production-faithful |
| ---------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| **SPA** (no SSR) | `bun run dev`          | `bun run preview`                         |
| **SSR · Bun**    | `bun run dev:bun`      | `bun run preview:bun`                     |
| **SSR · Node**   | `bun run dev:express`  | `bun run preview:express`                 |

The naming is systematic: the bare name is the **SPA**, the `:bun` / `:express`
suffix selects the **SSR runtime**, and the `dev` / `preview` prefix selects the
**mode**. Reach for `dev:*` while building — it is the fast inner loop, with HMR
and no build step — and for `preview:*` when verifying that the production bundle
behaves before a deploy: `preview:*` builds the client and runs a compiled
renderer over the built assets, the same artifact that deploys.

One asymmetry to expect in the **SPA** cells: this app is server-rendered, so
its `index.html` carries no `<title>`. The renderer re-emits that file's head
tags ahead of the ones React hoists, so a title there would beat every page's
in the SSR cells (see `@canonical/react-head`'s one-owner rule, and
`src/formatDocumentTitle.ts`). The SPA cells serve `index.html` directly, so the
tab is untitled for the moment before React renders the page's own title — and
stays untitled with JavaScript off. A scaffolded client-only app does not have
this: `summon` gives the `--rendering spa` arm a title in `index.html`, because it has no
server to compete with.

```bash
bun run storybook    # component workshop
```

The Relay schema and the compiler artifacts are committed, not rebuilt on the fly:

```bash
bun run schema         # regenerate src/relay/schema.graphql from the provider's ref packages
bun run relay          # regenerate src/relay/__generated__ after schema/query edits
bun run relay:watch    # the same, re-running on change — pair with dev:*
```

## Adding routes

`summon` scaffolds the building blocks of the app so new features follow the
established structure rather than diverging from it.

```bash
summon domain billing            # a new feature domain (routes + pages)
summon page billing/invoices     # a page within a domain, routed by hand
summon wrapper sidebar           # a layout wrapper
```

## Testing

```bash
bun run test          # unit + component tests (Vitest, jsdom)
bun run test:coverage # the same, with a coverage report
bun run test:e2e      # boots all six matrix servers and asserts each serves
```

`test:e2e` is an end-to-end test *of the build*: it runs each of the six server
scripts — including the production builds that `preview:*` performs — and asserts
that every server returns a rendered document and serves its client assets with
the correct content type.

## Project structure

```
src/
├── client/         Client entry (hydration)
├── server/         Server entry, compiled renderer, dev servers, sitemap, and
│                   `graph.ts` — TRANSPORT ONLY. The graph is not assembled
│                   here; it comes from @canonical/prism-pragma-provider.
├── domains/        Feature domains, each owning its routes, its layout,
│                   its pages and, in `lib/`, its components (see below).
├── lib/            Shared code: `ui/` (the shell, the site's rail and
│                   colophon, the prose page and the site's projections),
│                   `graph/` (the drawings' lattice and label cut),
│                   `markdown/` and `authGuard/`
├── i18n/           The app's message catalog and its translator hook
├── relay/          Relay environment factory, executable mock schema,
│                   and generated artifacts (__generated__/)
├── styles/         Application CSS
├── assets/         Assets imported in code (bundled and hashed by Vite)
└── routes.tsx      Root route map
public/             Files served verbatim at a fixed URL (favicon, robots.txt)
test/e2e/           The 2×3 server-matrix end-to-end suite
```

### Domains

| Domain | Routes | Archetype | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `marketing` | `/` | document | The lobby: a few components and a door per lens. |
| `components` | `/components`, `/components/:uri` | document | The catalog through the site's projections, and a component's page with its example, anatomy tree, properties and relations. |
| `definitions` | `/definitions`, `/definitions/:term` | workspace | The site's rail bound to `@canonical/prism-lens-definitions`'s layout. |
| `standards` | `/standards`, `/standards/:uri` | document | The site's rail and colophon bound to `@canonical/prism-lens-standards`'s layout. |
| `guides` | `/guides`, `/guides/:slug` | document | Guides as editorial prose. |
| `journeys` | `/journeys`, `/journeys/:job` | workspace | The demand model as a table, or as a graph of one coordinate's journeys with the job inspector. |
| `playground` | `/playground` | document | One component probed in every projection. |
| `account` | `/account`, `/login` | document | The demo sign-in and the account page. |
| `modifiers` | none | none | The modifier and modifier family projections. |

The core lenses are the `@canonical/prism-lens-*` packages and Guides:
every operation in them must execute against any provider implementing
`@canonical/prism-contract`, and the Standards lens's against any that also
serves the Prose extension (Tier 2); a gate in `prism-graph-example`
enforces both. `journeys` is a pragma-specific add-on: it reads pragma's
own ontology and makes no neutrality claim, and it is wired into
`routes.tsx` by hand until the docsite has a plugin mechanism (its
`index.ts` says why). `playground` carries one pragma-specific probe URI
(`probeQuery.ts`); it is neither a lens nor a declared add-on, so no gate
scans it.

Every component is scaffolded with the generator into `src/lib/ui/` or a
domain's `lib/`, with an `anatomy.yaml` written before its code: its slots,
cardinalities and style keys bound to tokens, transcribed into its
stylesheet. A component's private parts sit in its `common/` folder, and a
context provider follows the provider structure (`Provider.tsx`,
`Context.tsx`, `hooks/`). `src/testing/integration/anatomies.tests.ts`
checks every anatomy, its stylesheet and its scaffold, and the design's
token and grid rules in every stylesheet.

Domains are the unit of feature organisation: each owns its routes and pages, so
adding a feature is adding a domain rather than threading changes through shared
files. This app ships both `src/assets/` (assets imported in code) and `public/`
(files served by fixed URL); either may be removed if the app uses only one.

## Data layer (Relay)

The `components` domain demonstrates the app's [Relay](https://relay.dev) data
layer: the catalog's list runs `ComponentsCatalogQuery`, pages through its
`@connection` a hundred components at a time, and spreads the site's card and
row projections' fragments, each of which reads its own fields with
`useFragment`: a component owns its field selection, and the query that
fetches it only spreads it.

**The app needs a graph, and it runs as its own process.** `bun run graph`
(`src/server/graph.ts`) starts the pragma provider
([`@canonical/prism-pragma-provider`](../../../packages/prism/pragma-provider))
and serves its compiled schema at `http://127.0.0.1:5175/graphql` — nothing
else, no HTML. **The app assembles no provider of its own**: the ref-package
list and the compiler options live in that
package, and this app depends on no knowledge engine
(no `@canonical/ke`, no `@canonical/ke-graphql`). `graph.ts` is transport plus
one factory call. Every `dev*` / `preview*` script starts one for you via the
launcher (`src/server/withGraph.ts`), so in normal use you never run it by
hand. `createEnvironment` (`src/relay/environment.ts`) posts every operation
there; the address is decided in exactly one place
(`src/relay/graphqlEndpoint.ts`) and `VITE_GRAPHQL_URL` overrides it. Setting
that variable also tells the launcher an endpoint already exists, so it starts
no graph of its own — which is how you point the app at a shared or remote
one.

**Prerequisite:** `bun install`, and nothing else. The default provider
compiles from the ref packages it declares as dependencies, installed in
`node_modules`: the published design system, code standards and anatomy DSL,
and the docsite's demand model, which ships as two private shim packages in
[`packages/prism/semantics/`](../../../packages/prism/semantics) until it is
published. `PRAGMA_REFS_DIR` points it at a pragma refs cache instead, for
ontology branches that are not published yet. See
[the provider's README](../../../packages/prism/pragma-provider/README.md)
for the source layout it expects. This is a prerequisite of *that provider*,
not of this app: any provider implementing `@canonical/prism-contract` can take
its place — `@canonical/prism-graph-example` is a second one, written by
hand without the compiler — and set `VITE_GRAPHQL_URL`.

**The schema is generated, and gated.** `src/relay/schema.graphql` is what
relay-compiler validates every operation against. `bun run schema`
(`src/server/schema.ts`) writes it from one generated source: the SDL the
pragma provider emits over the ref packages it declares as dependencies, the
demand model's shims among them, so the journeys add-on's types are generated
like every other type and nothing is authored by hand. `bun run check` runs
`schema:check`, which regenerates and fails on a diff, so a schema change is
always a visible diff with a cause: a bumped ref package, a changed shim, or a
changed compiler. The graph server never writes this file, and serves exactly
what it holds (`src/server/committedSchema.tests.ts` boots the provider and
compares).

**Generated artifacts are committed.** The Vite plugin runs with
`codegen: false`, so `src/relay/__generated__/` is not rebuilt on the fly:
after editing a `graphql` tag or the schema, run `bun run relay` (or keep
`bun run relay:watch` running) to regenerate the artifacts, and commit them.

**Patched dependencies.** `patches/` carries two package patches applied via
`patchedDependencies` in `package.json` (a bun feature — with another package
manager, apply the equivalent mechanism): `react-relay@18.2.0` needs a
cjs-module-lexer export hint so named imports survive Node SSR, and
`relay-runtime-network@0.1.0` ships a broken `imports` map. The latter patch
is temporary until the fixed upstream release lands
([advl/lit-relay#32](https://github.com/advl/lit-relay/pull/32)); drop it and
its `patchedDependencies` entry once a fixed version is published.

**Not yet on npm.** `@canonical/storybook-addon-relay` and the fixed
`relay-runtime-network` release have not been published yet, so a fresh
install of this app will not fully resolve until they land on npm.

## Projections

The site renders every graph node in five forms, chip, row, card, command
and graph node, through `@canonical/prism-projections`. The `Shell` provides
the package's `defaultProjectionMaps`, so the lenses' mentions and indexes
dispatch as the package does. The design-system types the site's own graph
serves get projections of their own, one folder each under the domain
libraries, each filling the package's generic `Entity*` component from its
own Relay fragment and checked against its `anatomy.yaml`:

- `src/domains/components/lib/`: `UIBlockChip`, `UIBlockRow`, `UIBlockCard`,
  `UIBlockCommand` and `UIBlockGraphNode`, on the `UIBlock` interface, so one
  projection serves a component, a pattern and a layout; and
  `UIBlockExample`, the published React component a block's card renders in
  its sidecar, server-rendered, for a block the package implements.
- `src/domains/modifiers/lib/`: the `Modifier*` and `ModifierFamily*`
  projections.
- `src/domains/standards/lib/`: the `CodeStandard*` projections.

A projection reads only what its own fragment spreads, and the package's
composites spread only the contract's types, so the site dispatches these
types itself: `SiteChipProjection`, `SiteRowProjection`,
`SiteCardProjection`, `SiteCommandProjection` and `SiteGraphNodeProjection`
in `src/lib/ui/` each read a composite of the site's own. It spreads the
package's dispatcher of that form aliased as `Node`, and each design-system
projection aliased by the type it is on; the three UI-block types narrow to
their type with an aliased inline fragment
(`... on Component @alias(as: "Component") { ...UIBlockCard_node }`), so
each alias holds a key for its own type alone. `siteProjectionMaps`
(`src/lib/ui/constants.ts`) holds the arms by the same names and dispatches
through the package's `renderArm`: a design-system type renders through
its projection, and every other node through the package's dispatcher,
which renders ontology classes and any type the provided maps arm.

```tsx
import { SiteCardProjection } from "#lib/ui";

<SiteCardProjection node={node} />;
```

`src/testing/integration/projections.tests.ts` holds each composite's
aliases, its map's arms and its dispatcher anatomy's cases to one set, and
every projection's fragment to the fields its anatomy reads.

The site's own strings, these projections' words among them, come from its
catalog (`src/i18n/constants.ts`) through `useMessages` from `#i18n`, whose
default translator reads the English catalog.
